title: Product decomposition and geometric criteria for a diagonalizable group algebra
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $M$ be a finitely generated additive abelian group. Define $k[M]$ to have basis $e_m$ for $m\in M$, multiplication $e_me_n=e_{m+n}$, and Hopf operations $\Delta(e_m)=e_m\otimes e_m$, $\epsilon(e_m)=1$, $S(e_m)=e_{-m}$. Let $D_k(M)=\operatorname{Spec}k[M]$ be the associated affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. It is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If $M\simeq\mathbf Z^r\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^s\mathbf Z/n_i\mathbf Z$ with $r,s\geq0$ and $n_i\geq1$, there is an induced group-scheme isomorphism
$$D_k(M)\simeq\mathbf G_m^r\times_k\prod_{i=1}^s\mu_{n_i},$$
where $\mathbf G_m$ and $\mu_n=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]/(t^n-1)$ have the meanings of [def-sc-gm-ga]. In particular $D_k(\mathbf Z^r)\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$.

If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then $D_k(M)$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] if and only if $M$ has no nonzero element annihilated by a power of $p$; it is geometrically connected if and only if every finite-order element of $M$ is annihilated by a power of $p$. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $D_k(M)$ is smooth, and it is geometrically connected if and only if $M$ is torsion-free. Here geometrically connected means that every base change along a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], torsion-free means that $nm=0$ with an integer $n>0$ implies $m=0$, and the zero group and empty products are allowed.

source.place: Examples 12.1--12.2, Proposition 12.3, Lemma 12.4 and Remark 12.5, printed pp.231--232; Theorem 12.9(a), pp.233--234.

proof.text: Choose finitely many group generators $m_1,\ldots,m_d$ of $M$. The $2d$ elements $e_{m_j},e_{-m_j}$ generate $k[M]$ as an algebra: write any $m$ as an integer linear combination, separate its positive and negative coefficients, and multiply the corresponding basis elements. Thus its affine spectrum is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The Hopf identities hold on each $e_m$: both iterated coproducts are $e_m\otimes e_m\otimes e_m$, either counit gives $e_m$, and multiplication after the antipode gives $e_0=1$. By linearity these are the group-scheme identities [def-sc-group-scheme].

source.place: Section 12(b), printed p.231, the group-algebra construction (using generators and their negatives).

proof.text: For additive abelian groups $N,P$, the maps $e_{(n,p)}\mapsto e_n\otimes e_p$ and $e_n\otimes e_p\mapsto e_{(n,p)}$ extend to inverse algebra maps: the latter is induced by $e_n\mapsto e_{(n,0)}$, $e_p\mapsto e_{(0,p)}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], and the former is multiplicative on the displayed basis. Both composites fix every generator; the maps preserve coproduct, counit and antipode on these generators. Also $k[\mathbf Z]\cong k[t,t^{-1}]$ by $e_j\mapsto t^j$. For $n\geq1$, $k[\mathbf Z/n]\cong k[t]/(t^n-1)$ by $e_{\bar j}\mapsto t^j$; the inverse sends $t$ to $e_{\bar1}$, and $t$ is invertible with inverse $t^{n-1}$. Applying these maps to the given decomposition, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and [def-sc-gm-ga] give the claimed group-scheme product isomorphism. Empty tensor products are $k$.

For the criteria, choose a decomposition into a finite free group and finite cyclic groups using [lem-sbc-finitely-generated-abelian-group-structure] (a direct sum over a finite set is its finite product). Step 2 gives the coordinate presentation $A=k[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_r^{\pm1},t_1,\ldots,t_s]/(t_i^{n_i}-1)_i$. Successive applications of [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], over the preceding coefficient ring, give its Laurent-monomial and bounded-power basis: $x^v\prod_i t_i^{a_i}$, $v\in\mathbf Z^r$, $0\leq a_i<n_i$. In particular all these algebras are nonzero. For every field extension $K/k$, [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and the tensor universal property identify $K\otimes_k k[M]$ with $K[M]$, by $c\otimes e_m\mapsto ce_m$; the inverse sends $ce_m$ to $c\otimes e_m$. Thus this same presentation and basis hold after every field extension.

source.place: Proposition 12.3 and Remark 12.5, printed p.232; scalar extension is the explicit basis calculation.

proof.text: Suppose every $n_i$ is invertible in $k$ (automatic in characteristic zero). The presentation is finite, writing $x_j^{-1}$ as $y_j$ with relations $x_jy_j-1$. To verify formal smoothness [def-sbc-formally-smooth], take a first order thickening of affine schemes over $k$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]: $T'=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$ with $J^2=0$, $B$ a commutative $k$-algebra. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] a $k$-morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a $k$-algebra map $A\to B/J$, and an extension to $T'$ is a $k$-algebra map $A\to B$ lifting it. Each invertible $\bar x_j$ lifts to a unit $x_j$: lift its inverse too, and correct their product $1+z$, $z\in J$, by multiplying by $1-z$. Lift each $\bar t_i$ to $u_i$; then $u_i$ is a unit since $\bar t_i^{n_i}=1$. Set $a_i=u_i^{n_i}-1\in J$ and $v_i=u_i-a_i/(n_i u_i^{n_i-1})$. The square-zero binomial expansion gives $v_i^{n_i}=u_i^{n_i}-a_i=1$. Sending $t_i$ to $v_i$ gives the required lift. Finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] now give smoothness, including when there are no variables or equations.

source.place: Remark 12.5, printed p.232; explicit infinitesimal verification using Stacks Tag 02H0 (definition-formally-smooth).

proof.text: In characteristic $p>0$, if some $p\mid n_i$, the element $z=t_i^{n_i/p}-1$ of $A$ is nonzero by the bounded-power basis of step 3, while $z^p=t_i^{n_i}-1=0$. A smooth scheme over a field is geometrically reduced by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], hence reduced over $k$ itself; the displayed nonzero nilpotent rules out smoothness. In a finite cyclic group $\mathbf Z/n_i$, nonzero elements annihilated by a power of $p$ exist exactly when $p\mid n_i$: if $p\mid n_i$, the class $n_i/p$ has order $p$; if $p\nmid n_i$, multiplication by $p$ and every power of $p$ is invertible. The free factors have no such elements. Together with step 4 this proves the positive-characteristic smoothness equivalence and the unconditional characteristic-zero smoothness assertion.

source.place: Remark 12.5, printed p.232; Stacks Tag 056T (varieties, lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal).

proof.text: In characteristic $p>0$, suppose all finite cyclic orders $n_i$ are powers of $p$, allowing $n_i=1$. For every extension $K/k$ the coordinate ring in step 3 has relations $t_i^{n_i}-1=(t_i-1)^{n_i}$. The ideal $J=(t_i-1)_i$ is nilpotent: a product of $1+\sum_i(n_i-1)$ generators contains a factor $(t_i-1)^{n_i}$. Its quotient is $L=K[x_1^{\pm1},\ldots,x_r^{\pm1}]$, a domain: the polynomial ring $K[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is a domain by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-domain] and maps injectively to $L$ (Laurent-monomial basis); if $ab=0$ in $L$, multiply by a monomial to write $a=x^{-v}a'$, $b=x^{-v}b'$ with $a',b'$ polynomials, so $a'b'=0$ and $a=0$ or $b=0$. The quotient map $A_K\to L$ is surjective with nilpotent kernel, so [lem-pur-all-element-powers-spectrum-homeomorphism] applies (each element of $L$ is already in its image). Its spectrum is irreducible by [lem-zl-spectrum-irreducible-nilradical-prime], since the nilradical of a domain is the prime ideal $(0)$. Irreducibility implies connectedness: a decomposition into two nonempty clopens would be a decomposition into two proper closed subsets [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Hence $D_k(M)$ is connected after every field extension. In characteristic zero the same proof applies with no finite cyclic factors, giving geometric connectedness for torsion-free $M$.

source.place: Remark 12.5, printed p.232; Stacks Tags 0BR8 (algebra, lemma-powers) and 00ES (algebra, lemma-irreducible).

proof.text: Conversely take an algebraic closure $K$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. In characteristic $p>0$, write $n_i=p^{a_i}d_i$ with $p\nmid d_i$; in characteristic zero put $d_i=n_i$ and $p^{a_i}=1$ in the following calculation. The polynomial $T^{d_i}-1$ has $d_i$ distinct roots in $K$: repeated division by a linear root splits it, and its derivative $d_iT^{d_i-1}$ is nonzero at every root. In positive characteristic $T^{n_i}-1=\prod_{\zeta^{d_i}=1}(T-\zeta)^{p^{a_i}}$; in characteristic zero the same formula has exponent one. For distinct roots $(T-\zeta)-(T-\zeta')=\zeta'-\zeta$ is a unit, so the ideals $I_\zeta=((T-\zeta)^{p^{a_i}})$ are pairwise coprime (raise $1=a+b$ to the power $2p^{a_i}-1$). Hence $\bigcap_\zeta I_\zeta=\prod_\zeta I_\zeta=(T^{n_i}-1)$: for coprime $I,J$, $I\cap J=(I\cap J)(I+J)\subseteq IJ$, and $I$ is coprime to a product of ideals each coprime to it (multiply the relations $1=a_j+b_j$); induct on the number of roots. Applying [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] over the algebra in all other variables gives a product decomposition of $A_K$ with $d_i$ factors. Each factor is nonzero: set all $x_j=1$, all other $t_j=1$, and this $t_i=\zeta$ to map it to $K$. If $d_i>1$ this product has a nontrivial idempotent $e=(1,0,\ldots,0)$; $D(e)$ and $D(1-e)$ are nonempty disjoint clopens covering its spectrum, so the base change is disconnected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Finally the torsion of the free-plus-cyclic decomposition consists exactly of the finite cyclic factors. Every torsion element is killed by a power of $p$ exactly when all $d_i=1$, and in characteristic zero the group is torsion-free exactly when all $n_i=1$. This proves both connectedness equivalences. For $M=0$ all products are empty and the scheme is $\operatorname{Spec}k$, smooth and geometrically connected.

source.place: Remark 12.5, printed p.232; Stacks Chinese remainder theorem (algebra, lemma-chinese-remainder, Tag 00DT); explicit clopen decomposition.
